text.title: Value Proposition Design Core Rules
text.summary: 8 testable rules every Value Proposition Design application must enforce, plus a skip-this-methodology fallback. These are HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: Customer-profile jobs MUST cite ≥1 interview citation per job; un-cited jobs rejected.
rule.rationale: Un-cited jobs are founder projection, not customer reality.

rule.statement: Pains MUST describe friction in achieving the job; gains MUST describe outcomes wanted beyond the job — overlap is forbidden.
rule.rationale: Conflating pains and gains hides which side of the funnel each addresses.

rule.statement: Every pain-reliever MUST reference at least one pain id and every gain-creator MUST reference at least one gain id; orphan relievers and orphan creators are rejected. The reverse holds too: every pain needs ≥1 reliever and every gain ≥1 creator, or the entry is recorded as a known gap under r4.
rule.rationale: Relievers without pains are solutions in search of problems. Unpaired pains are unaddressed value and unpaired gains are wasted offer surface — the pairing in both directions is what makes the canvas a fit check rather than two lists.

rule.statement: Spec MUST list every pain/gain with no corresponding reliever/creator under an alignment_gaps array.
rule.rationale: Hidden gaps are the actual root cause of message rejection.

rule.statement: Value-prop statement MUST cite a named customer job; 'faster/easier/better' without job-anchor rejected.
rule.rationale: Adjective stacking is positioning theatre, not positioning.

rule.statement: Both canvas sides MUST be complete before the artefact is emitted: customer profile (jobs / pains / gains) AND value map (products / pain-relievers / gain-creators). One-sided canvases are rejected.
rule.rationale: A one-sided canvas is a feature list or a wishlist. The diagnostic value lives entirely in the pairing, so a half-filled canvas cannot produce the alignment gaps r4 requires.

rule.statement: The positioning statement MUST follow the Moore format: "For [segment] who [need], [product] is a [category] that [benefit]. Unlike [alternative], we [differentiator]." Taglines in place of the format are rejected.

rationale.source: Geoffrey Moore — Crossing the Chasm; April Dunford — Obviously Awesome

rule.rationale: A fixed format makes positioning statements comparable across products and stable across rewrites; copywriters derive marketing taglines downstream from it, not instead of it.

rule.statement: Each canvas artefact MUST address exactly one primary segment. Multi-segment canvases are split into one artefact per segment.
rule.rationale: Segments have different jobs, pains and gains; conflating them averages the canvas into generic copy that fits nobody.

rule.statement: If any Applies-If precondition fails OR any Skip-If condition triggers, do NOT apply this methodology. Emit a skip-record naming the failed precondition / triggered skip, and route the task to the correct methodology (or none).
rule.rationale: Mis-application produces worse artefacts than no methodology, because downstream consumers trust the schema; the skip-record makes non-application traceable.
